turnaround_reason: Charter collapsed ~65% from a ~$422 high to ~$150 as broadband subscribers bleed to fixed-wireless and fiber (down 172k in Q2 2026, a 4th straight quarterly revenue decline). It just closed the $34.5B Cox merger, making it the largest US internet/video provider at ~37M customers, and trades at a low-single-digit forward multiple with heavy insider buying.
bullish_points: Forward P/E ~3.4 on a large cash-generative franchise; classic levered FCF/buyback deleveraging setup
Cox merger closed — scale, ~12M mobile lines converging, and cost/synergy runway; Street mean target well above current price
Very strong insider buying: 1,672,194 shares purchased across 22 transactions vs 87,833 sold in last 6 months
Basing mode; deeply washed out after worst single-day drop ever, sentiment extremely negative
bearish_points: Secular broadband share loss is ongoing, not one-off — subs fell 120k in Q1 then 172k in Q2, worse than estimates
Extreme leverage: ~$96.7B total debt vs $509M cash (debt/equity ~442); refinancing risk if rates stay high
Revenue still declining (-1.7% YoY) with merger integration execution risk on top
Price sits ~19% below its 200d MA — no confirmed trend reversal yet
catalyst: Cox integration synergies + aggressive buybacks translating declining revenue into growing FCF/share, and any stabilization in broadband net adds (mobile bundle, rural build-out)
catalyst_timing: Next 2-4 quarters as merger synergies and mobile momentum show up; Q3/Q4 2026 broadband trend is the key tell
suggested_trade: Starter spot only, sized small given leverage. This is a levered FCF/buyback bet, not a growth story. Add on a confirmed inflection in broadband net adds.
key_risk: Broadband losses accelerate while $96B of debt has to be refinanced at higher rates, compressing equity value in a levered capital structure
would_skip_if: You're uncomfortable with 400%+ debt/equity, or broadband net losses widen further next quarter
